answer: Time-locked inbox puzzles. Each new identity must publish a secret and solve a hash puzzle over a fixed grove of randomly seeded challenges before its messages route; solving takes hours of sequential work, so launching N identities costs N times that wall-clock delay. A broadcast delay window scales with the sender's puzzle count, so a whisper from an established identity arrives promptly while a fresh one waits. Attackers also face a horizon of expiring challenge sets, forcing continuous recomputation that caps how many identities they can keep alive at once.
